title: Understanding Catastrophic Forgetting In LoRA via Mean-Field Attention Dynamics
claim: Small perturbations keep the model confined near the pretrained solution, while large perturbations or small spectral gaps trigger escape and forgetting.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, color-coded curves with red/blue annotations
description: Three line-plot panels illustrate the theoretical results schematically. Left: a 1-D energy landscape with a green dot for the pretrained weights. A short blue arrow (small LoRA, stable) stays in the basin, while a long red arc (large LoRA, catastrophic forgetting) jumps over the barrier. Middle: token position or clustering against depth. The base-model curve (black) and the LoRA-perturbed curve (red dashed) coincide inside a green shaded stability window, then split at a dotted bifurcation line T*. Black goes to Cluster A (correct) and red drops to Cluster B (forgot). Right: two parabolas over an eigenspace direction. A steep blue one (large spectral gap) gives robust confinement. A shallow orange one (small gap) gives easy escape. Red, blue and orange labels carry the contrast.
caption: Schematic representation of the theoretical results.
abstract: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) is the dominant parameter-efficient fine-tuning method due to its favorable compute-performance trade-off, yet it suffers from catastrophic forgetting. We study forgetting through a tractable _mean-field self-attention_ toy model, where tokens evolve as an interacting particle system and LoRA acts as a low-rank perturbation. Using tools from partial differential equations and dynamical systems, we characterize regimes suggesting a phase transition between forgetting and non-forgetting behavior. We show that one phase transition appears with respect to the norm of the perturbation, and the other with respect to the depth of the Transformers. We further bound the time-to-deviation in terms of the perturbation size and spectral quantities, and corroborate the predicted trends with experiments and exploratory analyses on real models under LoRA fine-tuning.
